extracted.intended_audience: researchers considering or preparing applications for ERC grants (EU and non-EU applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility criteria for preparing and submitting applications to the European Research Council's main grant schemes (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced, Proof of Concept, Synergy). Covers who the grants are for and pointers to application resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Starting Grants — eligibility and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers with 2-7 years of experience since the completion of their PhD, a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target early-career investigators (2–7 years post-PhD). Demonstrate a scientific track record that shows great promise and submit an excellent research proposal. Consult Work Programme and Information for Applicants for call-specific details and contact your National Contact Point for country-level help.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Consolidator Grants — eligibility and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers with 7-12 years of experience since completion of PhD, a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target mid-career investigators (7–12 years post-PhD). Emphasise growing independence and a strong research plan. Use official documents (Work Programme, Information for Applicants) to check any yearly call specifics and seek support from your National Contact Point.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Advanced Grants — eligibility and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for active researchers with a track-record of significant research achievements in the last 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target established, highly accomplished researchers. Evidence of significant research achievements in the past decade is required; proposals should reflect frontier-level research ambition. Refer to official call documentation for selection procedures and eligibility nuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Proof of Concept — eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers who have already received an ERC grant for their frontier research project and now want to explore the commercial or societal potential of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only previous ERC grantees are eligible. Focus is on translating or valorising previously funded ERC research toward commercial or societal applications; application scope differs from frontier research grants—check the Proof of Concept Work Programme text.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Synergy Grants — team composition and aims
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for two to maximum four researchers working together and bringing different skills and resources to tackle ambitious research problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate how multiple PIs with complementary skills/resources will jointly address an ambitious, high-risk/high-gain research challenge. Team composition limits (2–4 investigators) and collaborative justification are key—see call information for further rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-since-PhD eligibility windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for different ERC grant types is tied to the number of years since completion of the PhD (explicit ranges: 2–7 years for Starting, 7–12 years for Consolidator; Advanced uses recent achievements rather than a strict years-since-PhD window).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully verify your eligibility window for the call year. Some calls may have allowances (e.g., career breaks) detailed in the Work Programme or Information for Applicants—always consult those documents and your National Contact Point for country-specific interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific track record and proposal excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Across several ERC grants the page stresses a 'scientific track record showing great promise' (Starting/Consolidator) or 'track-record of significant research achievements' (Advanced) and expects an 'excellent research proposal'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should balance demonstrated past performance (publications, impact, achievements) with a clear, ambitious, well-written, frontier research proposal. Use call guidance documents to understand evaluation criteria and prepare evidence of independence and leadership where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the Work Programme and Information for Applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Key documents to refer to when considering applying include the Work Programme and the Information for Applicants, which 'highlight the specifics of the calls every year' and provide useful application information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents contain the formal eligibility rules, evaluation criteria, call deadlines, budget rules, submission procedures and call-specific nuances—read them closely for the relevant call year rather than relying on summary pages alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use National Contact Points for local applicant support
rubrics_metrics.description: National contact point: there is one based in every EU and Associated Country (and some countries outside Europe). They are designated to help applicants out in their own countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact your local National Contact Point early for practical guidance, interpretation of rules, and administrative questions. They can help with national-specific issues and point to local support services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequently Asked Questions as a practical resource
rubrics_metrics.description: The ERC has collected frequently asked questions over the years to guide applicants through the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the FAQs to resolve common procedural and eligibility questions quickly; they often reflect recurring applicant misunderstandings and practical clarifications not obvious from the Work Programme text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for non-EU researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a researcher from outside the ERC and you wish to apply, check out some of the things you should consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-EU applicants should review particular rules and practical considerations that may affect eligibility, host institution requirements, mobility, and administrative arrangements—seek guidance from the Information for Applicants and National Contact Points.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC explanatory videos and training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Step-by-step video and 'Erc classes' series (5 explanatory videos) provide concrete information about the ERC application process, including frequently made mistakes, tips and rumours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use videos and training materials to get an overview of the application steps, common pitfalls, and practical tips for preparing your proposal. They are complementary to, not a substitute for, the official written call documents.
